a:r.a:t: Examples of Nucleophilic Carbon-Carbon Bond Formation Reactions

p:cNvPr.descr: A diagram shows reactions of aldols, clasien ester, and decarboxylation of beta-keto acid. The first reaction is that of aldol condensation. On the left is a molecule containing 2 C. The left C bonds left to an R1 group, double bonds up to an O, and right to C. C bonds right to R2, which bonds down to H. The C has 2 red dots (representing electrons) and a red negative sign next to it. Electron transfer occurs to a pink molecule to the right, which consists of C bonded up to R3, down to R4, and double bonded right to O. Electron transfer occurs to the C, which occurs from the double bond to the O. To the right is an arrow with a convergent arrow showing the addition of H+; to the right of this, the 2 molecules have been combined. C double bonds up to O, left to R1, right to C, which bonds up to R2, down to H, and right to C, which is pink. C bonds up to R3, down to R4, and right to OH, the H of which is black, not pink. Below is the Clasien ester condensation reaction. A CoA-S bonds right to C, which double bonds up to O, and right to C, which bonds up and down to H. There are 2 electrons on the rightmost C, as well as a negative sign with a red arrow showing electron transfer to the C of the pink molecule to the right. It consists of C bonding up to R3, double bonding right to O, and down to S, which bonds right to R2. Electron transfer also occurs from the downward bond to the S. To the right is an arrow with a convergent-divergent arrow showing the addition of H+ and the removal of HS--R2. To the right, the product is CoA-S bonded right to C, which double bonds up to O and right to C, which bonds up and down to H, right to the pink C, up to R1, and double bonds right to O. Below, the final reaction shows the decarboxylation of a beta-keto acid. The reaction begins on the left with R bonded right to C, which double bonds up to O, and right to a blue shaded C. The blue shaded C bonds up and down to H, and right to a pink C, which double bonds up and right to a pink O and down and right to a pink O-. Electron transfer is shown from the minus sign to the bond just above the O, then from the rightmost pink C left to the blue shaded C. To the right is a right arrow with a convergent arrow showing the addition of H+. To the right, the product is composed of R bonded right to C, which double bonds up to O and right to C, which bonds up, down, and right to H. There is a + sign, and to the right of that, a pink CO2.
